sourceChanges.citationTitle: How to use AI as a teacher
Kunstig intelligens og GPT | University of Oslo

claimChanges.claimText: TSD-Autotekst is listed for University of Oslo in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: not specified.
NotebookLM is listed for University of Oslo in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: not specified.
Microsoft Foundry is listed for University of Oslo in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: not specified.
Microsoft Copilot Chat is listed for University of Oslo in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: not specified.
GPT UiO is listed for University of Oslo in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: not specified.
Gemini is listed for University of Oslo in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: not specified.
Autotekst is listed for University of Oslo in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: not specified.
UiO's student guidance presents AI as support rather than a replacement for the student's own work and tells students to show clearly when and how they used AI.
UiO tells students that permitted AI use varies between subjects and assignments, and that they should ask their teacher if they are unsure what is allowed.
UiO's teacher guidance says that when teachers allow AI use, they should provide clear AI-use guidelines and communicate academic integrity, accuracy, and source-use requirements to students.

UiO describes GPT UiO as a UiO-developed service for using AI models within UiO privacy requirements, and says GPT UiO can generally be used in teaching, research, and administrative tasks with data up to yellow (limited).

UiO recommends GPT UiO or Microsoft Copilot for students because, according to the student guidance, personal data and submitted data are not shared onward and conversations are not used to train future models.
